summary: Global equity markets are trading with cautious optimism as major indices touched record highs, though bearish options positioning in the Nasdaq 100 signals underlying skepticism even as analysts identify a technical buying anomaly in the index. The dominant macro driver is escalating Middle East tension, with Iran threatening to block the Strait of Hormuz, tanker attacks reaching their highest weekly frequency since the Iran conflict began, and Turkey deploying defensive support to Saudi Arabia against Houthi forces, collectively pressuring crude supply expectations despite the IEA announcing an accelerated release of 100 million barrels from strategic reserves. On the equity side, TJX is attracting renewed bullish sentiment driven by fresh consumer data, Nvidia and Microsoft's joint PC launch is generating tech sector interest, and Micron faces a divided Wall Street with some analysts calling for a triple-digit move while others remain skeptical. The principal risk factors dominating investor attention are Hormuz strait disruption threatening global oil flows, Iran's advancing uranium enrichment program adding geopolitical premium to energy markets, and domestic political uncertainty as Republicans distance themselves from Trump ahead of tight midterm races. In the short term, markets face a tug-of-war between resilient corporate narratives in tech and retail and a deteriorating geopolitical backdrop in the Gulf, suggesting elevated volatility with energy stocks likely outperforming while risk assets remain vulnerable to any escalation in the Strait of Hormuz.
